bullets.title: S&P on 9-week win streak; Tech P/E expanded to 48x from 32x since March lows
bullets.body: The S&P 500 has risen for 9 consecutive weeks—the longest streak in 40+ years—while Tech sector trailing 12-month P/E surged ~50% from ~32x at the 3/30 low to 48x. GS flags the market is rewarding beta/volatility over low-vol names, with the TMT Beta index outperforming the S&P Low Vol index. JPM momentum strategy remains overweight stocks, underweight bonds, with strong trend signals in Nasdaq, S&P500, and Nikkei; no reversals warranted yet pending short-term momentum crossover confirmation.

bullets.title: GOOGL raises $84.75B in massive equity offering to fund AI capex; 2027 capex to 'significantly increase'
bullets.body: Alphabet priced an upsized $84.75B equity raise (from $80B) comprising a secondary, $15B convertible preferred at 6.25%, and a $40B ATM program starting Q3 2026. Berkshire Hathaway invested $10B at a slight discount to market. Separately, GOOGL raised 2026 capex guidance to $180-190B and guided 2027 capex to 'significantly increase' vs. 2026, citing 'unprecedented internal and external demand for AI compute resources.' Gemini App reached 900M+ MAU.

bullets.title: Middle East escalation: oil at ~$96-98/bbl; Iran tensions drive energy/rate pressure
bullets.body: US-Iran conflict escalated with US strikes on Iranian targets and Iran launching missiles at Kuwait (one killed). Oil hit ~$98/bbl (+2%+ in pre-market), with markets pricing a potential near-term Straits of Hormuz reopening. Trump signaled Iran blockade could lift by Labor Day and claimed Iran agreed not to acquire nuclear weapons—Iran's Mehr news denied this. OECD warned of significant downside risk to global growth from a prolonged conflict; BOJ's Ueda noted Middle East turmoil could heighten inflation shock risk.

bullets.title: BOJ Governor Ueda turns hawkish: inflation risks tilted upside, June rate hike in play
bullets.body: BOJ Governor Ueda stated upside inflation risks are 'greater overall and likely to emerge sooner,' warned that delaying policy response risks forcing sharper hikes later, and said the BOJ will 'thoroughly discuss' raising rates if price risks outweigh economic downside—even amid Middle East uncertainty. Rengo wage growth of ~5% across firm sizes cited as supporting evidence. One analyst argues next BOJ hike is likely a standalone event, not the start of a sustained cycle.

bullets.title: AI capex driving 'chipflation': structural memory/HBM tightness seen lasting 2-3+ years
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's TMT note coins 'chipflation': AI infrastructure is absorbing 6x rising supply of HBM/DRAM/SSD/HDD, with hyperscalers using LTAs and prepayments creating a two-tier market favoring AI/cloud buyers over traditional customers. MU bull case PT $1,650 and SNDK $2,635 on structural memory tightness; MU expects $50B in buybacks FY27-28. SK Hynix previewed HBM4E at Computex with 48GB capacity and 4TB/s bandwidth.

bullets.title: ADP May jobs beat (+122k vs 118k est); JOLTS openings jumped to 7.6M, ratio above 1:1
bullets.body: ADP May private payrolls came in at 122k vs. 118k expected (fastest since April 2025), with small firms (<50 employees) adding 67k and large firms 40k; wage growth flat at 4.4%. JOLTS job openings surged in April to 7.6M vs. 6.8M consensus, with professional/business services hitting a 3-year high; the job openings-per-unemployed ratio ticked back above 1:1 to 1.03. 22V notes payroll data revisions are stabilizing and business formation remains healthy.

bullets.title: Trump proposes new tariffs on 60 countries over forced labor; 10% minimum on EU/Canada/Taiwan
bullets.body: The Trump administration proposed a new tariff round targeting 60 countries citing forced labor practices, including a 10% minimum on EU, Canada, Mexico, and Taiwan and 12.5% on China, Japan, and other major economies. This replaces Section 122 tariffs per one source. The EU says it remains on track to implement US-EU trade deal commitments by end of June.

bullets.title: Stablecoin arms race: Stripe/Visa/Mastercard near platform launch; Visa at $7B annualized settlement run rate
bullets.body: Stripe, Visa, and Mastercard are close to announcing a new stablecoin platform with Coinbase considering participation. Visa expanded stablecoin settlement to 9 blockchains with a $7B annualized run rate (up 50% QoQ) and launched USDC settlement with Cross River and Lead Bank. Mastercard is acquiring BVNK for up to $1.8B to expand digital asset infrastructure. KeyBanc sees Circle pressured by reduced default-issuer positioning.

bullets.title: Semis ripping on AI demand: MRVL +91-230% in weeks; SOX diverging from traditional ISM correlation
bullets.body: Marvell surged ~11% in pre-market (up ~230% in 2 months) after NVDA CEO Jensen Huang called it 'the next trillion-dollar company' at Computex; AVGO +2-3%, AMD +2.8%, INTC +6.7%. MRVL is also designing a networking chip for Google on Intel's 18A process for 2027 production. GS notes semis are diverging from historical ISM correlation in a structural way. The photonics basket gained +11.7% on the session.

bullets.title: AI debt now 15% of corporate bond market; JPMorgan sees AI investment surpassing global military spend by 2027
bullets.body: AI-related corporate debt now represents ~15% of the entire corporate bond universe, and JPMorgan forecasts AI investment will exceed global military spending by 2027. Meanwhile ~$300B in AI equity raises have been announced in the window. OpenAI's Codex reached 5M WAU (from near-zero in January), with enterprise revenue growing ~5% daily; compute constraints extend through 2032.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley: add risk via barbell of Cyclicals + Hyperscalers; earnings rebounded faster than expected
bullets.body: MS strategy (Wilson/Pauker) doubled down on positive 2026 outlook in early April, calling the durable market low and recommending a barbell of Cyclicals and Hyperscalers. Earnings have rebounded faster than consensus expected; small caps upgraded to overweight in November are up 18.1% YTD vs. S&P +11.1%. Russell 2000 aggregate earnings tracking 13% below expectations but revenues 2.7% above.

bullets.title: 22V warns AI demand beneficiaries face downside risk if margin expansion narrative breaks
bullets.body: 22V Research cautions that recent margin expansion may reflect post-slowdown labor/capital utilization rather than AI productivity, and that AI token costs are rising while organizations struggle to convert time savings into economic value. Uber capped AI tool usage on budget overruns. S&P 1500 margin sentiment is unusually high vs. deteriorating cost sentiment; a modest AI narrative shift could have outsized impact on momentum/AI capex beneficiaries.

bullets.title: Tech sector dominates 52-week highs; Health Care and Finance lagging
bullets.body: 73 stocks hit 52-week highs vs. 63 lows in the session, with Electronic Technology dominating (29 highs vs. 3 lows). AMD is up 362% YTD, MU +966%, WDC +1020%, STX +683%. Since the Oct 2022 bull market start, only Tech and Communication Services have outperformed the S&P 500; Health Care is the worst performer but still up 20%. Finance shows relative weakness: 7 highs vs. 12 lows.

bullets.title: SpaceX targets $75B IPO at $1.75T valuation; Wedbush puts 80%+ odds on Tesla-SpaceX merger by 2027
bullets.body: SpaceX is targeting a $75B IPO at $135/share (555.6M shares) implying a $1.75T valuation, with a roadshow beginning Thursday. Wedbush maintains 80%+ probability of a Tesla-SpaceX merger following the SpaceX IPO by 2027, citing growing operational ties and the joint Terafab initiative.

bullets.title: Private credit redemption stress: Partners Group caps withdrawals at 5% on $9B fund
bullets.body: Partners Group capped redemptions at 5% NAV quarterly on its $9B fund after large Q2 withdrawal requests, flagging broader wealth-channel outflow concerns across alternative asset managers. Pre-market, ARES fell 6.7%, KKR 6.4%, and BX 5.2% on the news; JPM frames the alts weakness as a buying opportunity, treating it as a lagging rather than leading indicator.

bullets.title: Bitcoin down 37% YoY vs. Nasdaq +41.5%; crypto 'bloodbath' as geopolitics and rate fears weigh
bullets.body: Bitcoin is diverging sharply from the AI-driven tech rally: Nasdaq 100 hit fresh record highs while Bitcoin is down 37% over the past 12 months and 48% below its prior-year peak. Bitcoin remains pressured by geopolitical tensions, ETF outflows, and rising rate fears.

bullets.title: Kuwait oil production to recover to 70% of normal in 6-8 weeks; gold falls 1% to $4,442
bullets.body: Kuwait Petroleum Company expects production to reach 70% of normal within 6-8 weeks and full recovery in ~4 months following Iranian missile strikes. Separately, spot gold fell ~1% to $4,442/oz. Russian oil-gas budget revenue dropped ~21% MoM to 678.9B rubles in May.

bullets.title: Labor's share of US GDP hits lowest level since 1947; consumer sentiment at all-time lows
bullets.body: Americans' labor compensation as a share of GDP fell to its lowest level since BLS tracking began in 1947, signaling structural income distribution shift toward capital. Separately, consumer sentiment hit all-time lows with 57% of respondents citing high prices as hurting finances (up from 50% in April), per Hedgeye data.

bullets.title: ERCOT Batch Zero approves 100 GW of large-load interconnection; AI data center energy demand accelerating
bullets.body: ERCOT voted to approve a batch interconnection process for large loads including data centers, with Batch Zero totaling 35 GW baseload and another 65 GW under study (100 GW total). US energy storage deployments are forecast to grow at 38% CAGR to 279 GWh annually by 2030. Liquid cooling advances (CoolIT validated 15kW cold plate vs. prior 4kW) extend the AI data center infrastructure runway.

bullets.title: Ward's vehicle sales rose to 16.08M in May; auto MSRP still 29% above pre-pandemic levels
bullets.body: Ward's total vehicle sales rose to 16.08M SAAR in May from 15.92M in April. New car average MSRP eased to $51,469 from a recent peak of $52,217 but remains 29% above the pre-pandemic May 2019 level of $39,711, suggesting structural price stickiness in autos.
